description: Per-grain stochastic switching in granular high-anisotropy media, assembled from components. The field's word for this is 'stochastic switching'; run as a composition it is three independent terms - a thermodynamic noise floor, a weak helicity-selective bias, and a grain-to-grain variance - each with a different escape route. The composed option (deterministic single-pulse writing of granular media) does not exist; every component is known, and the composition fails at the bias term, not the noise term.

components.name: thermal activation over the anisotropy barrier (Néel/Arrhenius)
components.law: at full demagnetization the per-grain reversal probability approaches 0.5 - a coin flip; this is the noise floor and it is thermodynamic

components.name: MCD helicity bias (~2-5% absorption asymmetry)
components.law: magnetic circular dichroism; orientation-dependent absorption delta_pm = 1 +/- Delta/2 produces different per-pulse switching rates P(F delta_+), P(F delta_-)

components.name: fluence window (8-16 mJ/cm2 in FePt)
components.law: below threshold no switching; at ~9.5 mJ/cm2 maximal induced magnetization; at ~14 mJ/cm2 full demagnetization (p -> 0.5); above ~16 mJ/cm2 prolonged above-T_C randomization and damage

components.name: pulse accumulation (10^3-10^4 excitations per grain)
components.law: reptation: ensemble creeps to steady state m_inf = (P_- - P_+)/(P_- + P_+) with time constant ~1/(delta P); each grain excited ~1000-10000 times at 1 kHz sweeps

components.name: grain-to-grain variance (size and absorption distributions)
components.law: the reptation model averages over grains, but deterministic ensemble writing requires the minimum over grains, not the mean: 10-20% of FePt nanoparticles were unswitchable due to near-field absorption variance (XFEL study)

components.name: IFE effective field (inverse Faraday effect)
components.law: optically induced magnetic moment; deterministic switching region exists but requires ~10 T for ~0.6 ps or ~60 T for ~0.2 ps - in FePt the required fluence exceeds the damage threshold, so this term does not hold under load at sub-damage fluence

rejected.option: single-pulse MCD-driven switching of granular media
rejected.ruled_out_by: bias-to-noise ratio: a 2-5% absorption asymmetry cannot decide a 50% coin flip in one trial; John et al. 2017 state it directly - 'single shot will never be achieved with MCD'

rejected.option: single-pulse IFE switching of granular FePt at recording-relevant grain sizes
rejected.ruled_out_by: damage threshold: deterministic IFE needs tens of Tesla effective fields (10 T for 0.6 ps, or 60 T for 0.2 ps); the fluence required in FePt exceeds the damage threshold of the medium

rejected.option: pure thermal (helicity-independent) deterministic writing of granular media
rejected.ruled_out_by: noise floor: heating alone randomizes - at full demagnetization every grain is an unbiased coin flip; heat is the write enabler, not the write selector

budget_terms: fluence window between switching threshold and damage threshold
pulse count per grain (time budget at fixed repetition rate)

diagnostic.note: the multiscale models (Ellis 2016 reptation; John 2017) identified the mechanism split: MCD gives a probability bias, IFE gives a deterministic torque; the composition fails at the bias term, not the noise term. The models do not close the question - they locate the wall

source_class: collected - published models and experiments (Ellis et al. arXiv:1605.00835; John et al. Sci. Rep. 7, 4114 (2017); Lambert et al. Science 345, 1337 (2014); dual-pulse arXiv:1903.01941; XFEL grain-variance study)
open: the noise floor is thermodynamic and fixed; the bias term is optical and engineerable - microcavity-enhanced IFE (giant peak in magnetophotonic band gap, Sci. Rep. 2018) and plasmonic antennas are the adjacent-field bias amplifiers; Oppeneer's group: 'a technical challenge, not a fundamental obstruction'

dual-pulse fs-demagnetize + ps-steer works deterministically in continuous Pt/Co/Pt (4 pulse pairs) but is untested in granular media - whether a ps circular pulse can bias isolated grains without re-demagnetizing them is the open experiment

the variance term is the HDD industry's daily manufacturing problem (grain size distributions, heat-sink layers) - deterministic ensemble writing requires the tail of the distribution, not the mean the reptation model averages over

CrPt (easy-plane antiferromagnet) shows coherent nonthermal IFE switching within a few hundred fs - the material-class variable (magnetooptical response strength) may be the real scope condition on 'IFE cannot do it'
